news.n_byz_858: A layman, Photios, the most learned man alive, has been made patriarch after being rushed through every rank of the clergy in six days.
news.n_byz_860: News has come that an unknown people called the Rus attacked the suburbs of Constantinople in two hundred boats and sailed off with their loot.
news.n_byz_864: They say Prince Boris of Bulgaria has been baptized, with Emperor Michael himself as his godfather.
news.n_byz_867: Emperor Michael has been murdered in the palace at night. Basil, a former groom from Macedonia, has taken the throne.
news.n_byz_869: A council has opened in the capital to condemn Photios. The aged Ignatios has been restored to the patriarchal throne.
news.n_byz_872: News from the east: the emperor's army has crushed the Paulicians, and their leader Chrysocheir is dead. Their fortress of Tephrike has fallen.
news.n_byz_876: In Italy the city of Bari, taken back from the Saracens, has surrendered to the Roman governor.
news.n_byz_880: In the capital Emperor Basil's New Church has been consecrated, its five domes gleaming with gold.
news.n_byz_883: People whisper that Emperor Basil, misled by slander, has imprisoned his heir Leo. The whole court is pleading for the young man.
news.n_byz_886: Emperor Basil has died after a hunting accident. His heir Leo, already called the Wise, now rules.
news.n_byz_889: They say Emperor Leo writes books: military manuals, sermons, even poems.
news.n_byz_892: Lawyers in the capital are rendering Justinian's old laws into Greek: the emperor has ordered them gathered into a single code, the Basilika.
news.n_byz_896: Disaster: the army has been beaten by the Bulgarians at Boulgarophygon, and the empire will have to pay Symeon tribute.
news.n_byz_899: The court has drawn up a new list of ranks: who stands behind whom at receptions and who is paid what.
news.n_byz_902: Taormina, the last Roman fortress in Sicily, has fallen.
news.n_byz_904: Terrible news: the Saracen fleet of Leo of Tripoli has taken and sacked Thessalonica. Tens of thousands have been carried off.
news.n_byz_907: There are rumors that Oleg, prince of the Rus, came up to the capital and the emperor paid him to leave.
news.n_byz_911: A treaty has been made with the Rus: their merchants will lodge at Saint Mamas and receive bread, wine and baths at the treasury's expense.
news.n_byz_913: Emperor Alexander has died after a banquet and a ball game. Seven-year-old Constantine, born in the Purple Chamber, now reigns.
news.n_byz_917: By the river Achelous Symeon's Bulgarians destroyed a huge Roman army. They say the bones of the fallen still lie there.
news.n_byz_920: Romanos Lekapenos, admiral of the fleet, has become father-in-law and co-emperor to the young Constantine. They say he will soon be senior emperor.
news.n_byz_923: Off Lemnos the fleet has defeated the ships of Leo of Tripoli, the sacker of Thessalonica.
news.n_byz_927: Tsar Symeon is dead. His heir Peter has made peace and married Emperor Romanos's granddaughter.
news.n_byz_931: Christopher, eldest heir of Emperor Romanos, has died. The emperor, they say, is inconsolable.
news.n_byz_934: After years of war John Kourkouas has taken Melitene. Meanwhile the Magyars have raided as far as Thrace.
news.n_byz_938: Emperor Romanos has issued another law against the magnates: the poor who sold their land in the famine may buy it back at the old price.
news.n_byz_941: Prince Igor of the Rus attacked the capital with a vast fleet, but Greek fire burned his boats.
news.n_byz_944: The Image of Edessa, the cloth bearing the face of Christ not made by human hands, has been brought to the capital in triumph. The whole city went out to meet it.
news.n_byz_945: The Lekapenoi have been tonsured and exiled to the islands. Constantine Porphyrogennetos rules in his own right at last.
news.n_byz_949: The expedition against Crete has failed: the Saracens fell on the camp, and the fleet came home empty-handed.
news.n_byz_953: In the east the Hamdanid Sayf al-Dawla has beaten the domestic Bardas Phokas again. The old general was wounded in the face.
news.n_byz_957: Princess Olga of the Rus has been received at the palace. They say she was baptized in Constantinople.
news.n_byz_961: Nikephoros Phokas has taken Chandax! Crete, a pirates' nest for a century and a half, is ours again.
news.n_byz_963: The army has proclaimed Nikephoros Phokas emperor. On Athos his friend Athanasios is building the Great Lavra.
news.n_byz_965: Tarsus in Cilicia and the island of Cyprus have been taken. The gates of Tarsus are being carried to the capital as a trophy.
news.n_byz_969: The army has taken Antioch. And in December Emperor Nikephoros was murdered in his bedchamber, and John Tzimiskes took the throne.
news.n_byz_972: The emperor's niece Theophano has been married to Otto, heir of the German emperor.
news.n_byz_975: Emperor John has made a victorious march through Syria as far as Lebanon. They say he saw the Sea of Galilee.
news.n_byz_979: The Skleros revolt is over: Bardas Phokas and the Georgian allies defeated him, and the rebel fled to the Arabs.
news.n_byz_982: In Italy the Saracens have defeated the German emperor Otto. They say he saved himself by swimming out to a ship.
news.n_byz_986: Disaster in Bulgaria: at the Gates of Trajan Emperor Basil's army was ambushed, and he barely escaped.
news.n_byz_988: They say Prince Vladimir of the Rus has been baptized and received the princess Anna as his wife, and his Varangians have come to help the emperor.
news.n_byz_989: The rebel Bardas Phokas died in battle at Abydos. And in autumn an earthquake brought down part of the dome of Hagia Sophia.
news.n_byz_992: The emperor has lowered the duties on Venetian ships; Venice has promised to transport Roman troops.
news.n_byz_995: Emperor Basil moved his army across Anatolia in sixteen days and saved Aleppo from the Fatimids.
news.n_byz_997: On the river Spercheios Nikephoros Ouranos crushed the army of Tsar Samuel of Bulgaria.
news.n_byz_1001: A ten-year truce has been made with the Fatimid caliph. Trade with Egypt will revive.
news.n_byz_1005: Dyrrachion on the Adriatic has gone over to Emperor Basil.
news.n_byz_1009: The pilgrims are horrified: the Egyptian caliph al-Hakim has ordered the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem destroyed.
news.n_byz_1011: In Italy the revolt of Melus has been crushed: the katepan has entered Bari again.
news.n_byz_1014: At Kleidion Emperor Basil defeated the Bulgarians. They say Tsar Samuel died at the sight of his blinded soldiers.
news.n_byz_1018: Bulgaria is conquered: Emperor Basil has entered Ohrid in triumph. In Italy rebels and Norman mercenaries were defeated at Cannae.
news.n_byz_1022: The Armenian kingdom of Vaspurakan has placed itself under the emperor; its king received lands in Cappadocia.
news.n_byz_1025: Emperor Basil, the scourge of the Bulgarians, is dead. He reigned almost fifty years and left the treasury full.
news.n_byz_1028: Emperor Constantine has died, and his daughter Zoe, at fifty, has married Romanos Argyros, who is now emperor.
news.n_byz_1030: Emperor Romanos marched on Aleppo and fled from the Arabs, losing his baggage. The markets laugh at him.
news.n_byz_1034: Emperor Romanos has drowned in his bath. The same day Zoe married the young Michael the Paphlagonian.
news.n_byz_1038: Maniakes has landed in Sicily. Varangians fight with him, among them, they say, a Norwegian prince called Harald.
news.n_byz_1042: The people of the capital have overthrown Emperor Michael the Caulker for banishing Zoe. Zoe and her sister Theodora now rule.
news.n_byz_1045: Ani, the Armenian capital, has been annexed to the empire.
news.n_byz_1048: Alarming news from the east: the Seljuk Turks have ravaged Armenia and burned the rich town of Artze.
news.n_byz_1050: Empress Zoe has died. The City mourned her as the last of a great dynasty.
news.n_byz_1054: The Roman legates excommunicated Patriarch Michael, and he anathematized them in turn.
news.n_byz_1055: They say the Seljuk sultan Tughril Beg has entered Baghdad and rules in the caliph's name.
news.n_byz_1059: Isaac Komnenos has become a monk. The emperor is now Constantine Doukas, a friend of the scholar Psellos.
news.n_byz_1061: News from the west: the Normans have crossed to Sicily and taken Messina.
news.n_byz_1064: The Seljuks have taken Ani. They say the city ran with blood.
news.n_byz_1068: The widowed empress has married the general Romanos Diogenes. He promises to stop the Turks.
news.n_byz_1071: Terrible news: the army has been beaten at Manzikert, and Emperor Romanos is the sultan's prisoner.
news.n_byz_1074: They say the Roman pontiff Gregory is calling on the Latins to go to the aid of the eastern Christians against the Turks.
news.n_byz_1078: The old general Nikephoros Botaneiates has entered the capital and become emperor.
news.n_byz_1081: Alexios Komnenos has taken the capital, and his soldiers plundered the city for three days. Robert Guiscard's Normans beat him at Dyrrachion.
news.n_byz_1085: Robert Guiscard, the terror of the Romans, has died of fever on Kephalonia.
news.n_byz_1087: The Pechenegs have defeated Emperor Alexios at Dristra on the Danube. Thrace is in danger.
news.n_byz_1091: At the hill of Levounion Emperor Alexios and the Cumans destroyed the Pecheneg horde. Thanksgiving services are held all over Thrace.
news.n_byz_1092: The emperor has issued a new gold coin, the hyperpyron. The old debased nomismata are no longer accepted.
news.n_byz_1095: They say the Roman pontiff Urban called on the Franks at a council in Clermont to go and free Jerusalem.
news.n_byz_1097: Nicaea is ours again: the crusaders besieged it, but it surrendered to the emperor's men.
news.n_byz_1099: The crusaders have taken Jerusalem. They say there was a terrible massacre in the streets.
news.n_byz_1101: A new Latin army bound for the Holy Land has been wiped out by the Turks in Anatolia.
news.n_byz_1104: The Norman Bohemond, prince of Antioch, has sailed west to raise an army against the empire.
news.n_byz_1108: At Dyrrachion Bohemond has surrendered and signed a peace: Antioch recognizes the emperor's authority.
news.n_byz_1111: The Pisans too have received trading privileges and their own landing place in the capital. The Venetians are not pleased.
news.n_byz_1113: The Turks came up to Nicaea, but Emperor Alexios defeated them on their way back.
news.n_byz_1116: At Philomelion Emperor Alexios defeated the Seljuks and led thousands of Christians out of Anatolia with him.
news.n_byz_1118: Emperor Alexios has died. His heir John reigns, called the Beautiful for his goodness rather than his looks.
news.n_byz_1122: At Beroia Emperor John has crushed the Pechenegs. The prisoners were settled on empty lands.
news.n_byz_1126: The Venetian fleet raided the islands until the emperor restored Venice's trading privileges.
news.n_byz_1130: Emperor John has marched again against the Danishmendids in Paphlagonia.
news.n_byz_1133: Emperor John has taken Kastamon from the Danishmendids and returned to the capital in triumph.
news.n_byz_1136: In the capital a fifty-bed hospital with physicians and a pharmacy has opened at the Pantokrator monastery.
news.n_byz_1140: Emperor John's winter campaign against Neocaesarea has failed: the horses died of cold.
news.n_byz_1143: Emperor John died while hunting in Cilicia, wounded by his own arrow. The youngest heir, Manuel, now reigns.
news.n_byz_1147: The Germans and French of the Second Crusade have marched through the empire. Meanwhile the Normans of Sicily sacked Thebes and Corinth and carried off the silk weavers.
news.n_byz_1149: The island of Corfu has been retaken from the Normans.
news.n_byz_1153: Emperor Manuel loves Latin customs: knightly tournaments are held at court, and he breaks lances himself.
news.n_byz_1155: A Roman army has landed in Italy and taken Bari. The emperor dreams of recovering the ancient lands.
news.n_byz_1159: Emperor Manuel made a ceremonial entry into Antioch, while the king of Jerusalem walked on foot beside his horse.
news.n_byz_1162: The Seljuk sultan Kilij Arslan stayed in the capital for three months. He was taken to the Hippodrome and showered with gifts.
news.n_byz_1165: The emperor's cousin Andronikos Komnenos has escaped from prison and taken refuge with the prince of Galich in Rus.
news.n_byz_1169: A Roman fleet with the king of Jerusalem besieged Damietta in Egypt but left empty-handed.
news.n_byz_1171: On a single day the Venetians were arrested throughout the empire and their goods confiscated. Venice threatens revenge.
news.n_byz_1175: Emperor Manuel has rebuilt the fortress of Dorylaion on the Seljuk frontier.
news.n_byz_1176: At Myriokephalon the sultan lured Manuel's army into a gorge and beat it. The emperor compared it to Manzikert.
news.n_byz_1180: Emperor Manuel has died. His heir Alexios is only eleven, and the fight over the regency has already begun.
news.n_byz_1182: In the capital a mob has massacred the Latins in their quarter. The Genoese and Pisans are fleeing by sea.
news.n_byz_1185: The Normans have taken and sacked Thessalonica. In the capital the people tore Andronikos to pieces, and Isaac Angelos became emperor.
news.n_byz_1189: The German emperor Frederick Barbarossa is marching through Thrace to the Holy Land, plundering as he goes.
news.n_byz_1191: King Richard of England has seized Cyprus on his way to the Holy Land.
news.n_byz_1195: Alexios Angelos has blinded Emperor Isaac and taken the throne himself.
news.n_byz_1197: To buy off the German emperor a special "Alamanikon" tax has been imposed. They say gold was stripped even from the imperial tombs.
news.n_byz_1200: They say another crusade is gathering in the west, and the Venetians are building ships for it.
news.n_byz_1204: Constantinople has been taken and sacked by the Latins. There is a Latin emperor there now.
news.n_byz_1208: Theodore Laskaris has been crowned in Nicaea. The Romans have their own emperor again.
news.n_byz_1211: At Antioch on the Maeander Emperor Theodore Laskaris defeated the Seljuks, and the sultan fell in battle.
news.n_byz_1214: The Seljuks have taken Sinope from Trebizond. And peace with the Latins has been signed at Nymphaion.
news.n_byz_1217: The new Latin emperor, Peter of Courtenay, was seized in the mountains of Epirus. He was never seen again.
news.n_byz_1219: Emperor Theodore Laskaris has married the Latin princess Maria of Courtenay. There is peace with the Latins.
news.n_byz_1222: Theodore Laskaris has died in Nicaea. His son-in-law John Vatatzes is emperor.
news.n_byz_1224: Theodore Doukas, ruler of Epirus, has driven the Latins out of Thessalonica.
news.n_byz_1225: Vatatzes's troops have crossed into Thrace and briefly occupied Adrianople.
news.n_byz_1229: They say the German emperor Frederick obtained Jerusalem from the Egyptian sultan without a fight, by treaty.
news.n_byz_1232: The patriarch in Nicaea is corresponding with the Roman pontiff about uniting the churches. Few expect success.
news.n_byz_1235: Vatatzes and Tsar Asen of Bulgaria together besieged Latin Constantinople but could not take it.
news.n_byz_1238: Rumors come from the north of a terrible people, the Tatars, who are burning the Rus cities one after another.
news.n_byz_1241: They say the Tatars have beaten the Hungarians and Poles and reached the Adriatic Sea itself.
news.n_byz_1243: The Mongols have crushed the Seljuks at Köse Dağ. The sultan of Konya is now their tributary.
news.n_byz_1246: John Vatatzes has entered Thessalonica without a fight: the city is now under Nicaea.
news.n_byz_1250: Merchants say the French king Louis was captured in Egypt, where the Mamluks have seized power.
news.n_byz_1254: Emperor John Vatatzes, whom the people call the Merciful, has died. His heir Theodore, learned and sickly, reigns.
news.n_byz_1258: The Mongols have taken and ravaged Baghdad, and the caliph is dead. In Nicaea Michael Palaiologos has become regent for the boy John.
news.n_byz_1261: Constantinople is ours again! The Latin emperor has fled, and Michael Palaiologos has entered the City.
news.n_byz_1262: The Latin prince of Achaea, to buy his release from captivity, has handed Mystras and Monemvasia to the emperor.
news.n_byz_1266: Charles of Anjou, the French king's brother, has seized Sicily. They say he dreams of Constantinople.
news.n_byz_1270: King Louis of France has died of plague outside Tunis. The feared expedition against Constantinople will not take place.
news.n_byz_1274: The emperor's envoys at Lyon have accepted Rome's authority over the Church. The monks are muttering.
news.n_byz_1277: The Egyptian sultan Baybars has defeated the Mongols in Anatolia and briefly entered Kayseri.
news.n_byz_1281: At Berat in Albania the army of Charles of Anjou has been defeated, and its general captured.
news.n_byz_1285: Emperor Andronikos has disbanded the fleet to save money. The Genoese and the pirates now rule the sea.
news.n_byz_1287: An envoy of the Mongol ilkhan visited the capital: Sauma, a Christian monk from distant Cathay.
news.n_byz_1291: The Mamluks have taken Acre, the last Latin stronghold in the Holy Land.
news.n_byz_1295: They say the Venetian Marco Polo has returned home after twenty years with the Great Khan.
news.n_byz_1299: Emperor Andronikos has married the five-year-old princess Simonis to King Milutin of Serbia for the sake of peace.
news.n_byz_1303: Roger de Flor's Catalan mercenaries have sailed into the capital to fight the Turks for pay.
news.n_byz_1305: Roger de Flor has been killed at the palace by Alan mercenaries. The Catalans swear revenge.
news.n_byz_1309: The Knights Hospitaller have seized Rhodes and are settling in for good.
news.n_byz_1311: The Catalans have defeated the duke of Athens and seized the city.
news.n_byz_1315: The grand logothete Theodore Metochites is restoring the Chora monastery: new mosaics are covering its walls.
news.n_byz_1317: The Ottomans have surrounded Prousa on all sides: neither merchant nor peasant can get into the town.
news.n_byz_1321: The old emperor Andronikos and young Andronikos the Younger are fighting for power. Thrace is split into two camps.
news.n_byz_1325: Andronikos the Younger has been crowned co-emperor. The peace between the two Andronikoi is shaky.
news.n_byz_1329: At Pelekanos Emperor Andronikos was defeated by the Ottomans and wounded.
news.n_byz_1331: Nicaea has surrendered to Orhan. They say the city was handed over without a massacre.
news.n_byz_1334: The Moroccan traveler Ibn Battuta, who has seen half the world, passed through the capital. He was taken to see Hagia Sophia.
news.n_byz_1337: Nicomedia has fallen. The Romans no longer hold a single town in Bithynia.
news.n_byz_1341: Emperor Andronikos III has died. His heir John is nine years old, and Kantakouzenos is quarrelling with the regents over power.
news.n_byz_1345: The all-powerful Alexios Apokaukos has been killed by prisoners in the very prison he was building.
news.n_byz_1347: Terrible news comes from the ports: a plague has come on the Genoese ships, and people die within three days.
news.n_byz_1349: The Genoese of Galata burned the emperor's new fleet right in the Golden Horn.
news.n_byz_1352: The Ottomans have occupied the fortress of Tzympe on the Gallipoli peninsula, their first stronghold in Europe.
news.n_byz_1354: An earthquake brought down the walls of Gallipoli, and the Ottomans settled the town. Emperor John Kantakouzenos has abdicated and become a monk.
news.n_byz_1357: Pirates kidnapped Halil, Orhan's son. Emperor John ransomed him, hoping to win the sultan's favor.
news.n_byz_1359: A Turkish band has appeared beneath the very walls of Constantinople for the first time.
news.n_byz_1362: Sultan Orhan has died. His heir Murad is campaigning in Thrace.
news.n_byz_1366: Count Amadeus of Savoy and his crusaders have retaken Gallipoli from the Turks.
news.n_byz_1369: Emperor John V has converted to the Latin faith in Rome, hoping for Western help. No help is in sight yet.
news.n_byz_1373: Andronikos, the emperor's heir, rebelled together with the sultan's son. The revolt was crushed and the rebels blinded.
news.n_byz_1376: Andronikos IV has seized the capital with Genoese help and imprisoned the emperor.
news.n_byz_1379: John V has escaped from prison and regained the throne with Turkish help.
news.n_byz_1383: The Ottomans have laid siege to Thessalonica. The despot Manuel swears to hold out.
news.n_byz_1387: Thessalonica has surrendered to the Ottomans after a four-year siege.
news.n_byz_1391: John V has died. The emperor is now Manuel II, a scholar and a soldier.
news.n_byz_1394: Sultan Bayezid has laid siege to Constantinople by land.
news.n_byz_1396: At Nikopolis on the Danube the Turks routed a huge crusader army.
news.n_byz_1400: Emperor Manuel is in Paris and London asking for help. They say the Latin kings are amazed at his learning.
news.n_byz_1402: Timur has defeated and captured Sultan Bayezid at Ankara! The siege of Constantinople has been lifted.
news.n_byz_1403: By the treaty of Gallipoli Bayezid's sons have given Thessalonica back to the empire.
news.n_byz_1407: Theodore, despot of the Morea, has died. Emperor Manuel wrote the funeral oration himself.
news.n_byz_1411: Bayezid's son Musa besieged Constantinople, but the city held.
news.n_byz_1415: Emperor Manuel has rebuilt the Hexamilion, the wall across the Isthmus of Corinth, in a month.
news.n_byz_1419: They say the Romans are keeping a pretender, Mustafa, who calls himself Bayezid's son, on Lemnos, in case of war with the sultan.
news.n_byz_1421: Sultan Mehmed has died. The new sultan, Murad II, is young and, they say, bears a grudge against the Romans.
news.n_byz_1425: Emperor Manuel II has died. John VIII reigns.
news.n_byz_1428: The emperor's brothers, the despots of the Morea, are winning back almost the whole Peloponnese from the Latins.
news.n_byz_1430: Sultan Murad has stormed Thessalonica. The city has been sacked.
news.n_byz_1434: In Mystras the old philosopher Plethon teaches; he talks of Plato as if he were alive.
news.n_byz_1437: The emperor, the patriarch and hundreds of bishops have sailed for Italy to a council on uniting the churches.
news.n_byz_1439: Union with Rome has been signed in Florence. Mark of Ephesus refused to sign.
news.n_byz_1443: The Hungarian John Hunyadi is beating the Turks in the Balkans, and in Albania Skanderbeg has risen against the sultan.
news.n_byz_1446: Sultan Murad has smashed the Hexamilion with cannon and ravaged the Morea.
news.n_byz_1449: Constantine XI has been crowned in Mystras. He reached the capital on a Catalan ship.
news.n_byz_1452: Sultan Mehmed has built a fortress on the Bosporus in five months, the "Throat-Cutter".
news.n_byz_1453: Constantinople has fallen. The last emperor, Constantine, died on the walls, and Hagia Sophia has become a mosque.
news.n_byz_1456: At Belgrade Hunyadi has beaten back Sultan Mehmed's army.
news.n_byz_1458: The Ottomans have taken Athens. They say the sultan admired the Parthenon.
news.n_byz_1460: The sultan has conquered the Morea. The despot Thomas fled to Italy with the head of the Apostle Andrew.
news.n_byz_1461: Trebizond has surrendered to the sultan. The last Roman realm is no more.
news.n_byz_1470: The Ottomans have taken the island of Euboea, Negroponte, from Venice.
news.n_byz_1475: The Ottomans have taken Genoese Kaffa in the Crimea. The Black Sea has become a Turkish lake.
news.n_byz_1481: Sultan Mehmed, the conqueror of Constantinople, has died.
